claim: The Drosophila motor system is organized into anterior-posterior repeated, left-right symmetrical hemisegments.
source: The Drosophila motor system is organized into anterior-posterior repeated, left-right symmetrical hemisegements (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated directly in text and illustrated in Figure 1A showing the segmental organization of the larval body.

claim: Each hemisegment contains 30 muscle cells that are organized into three main groups—dorsal, transverse, and ventral.
source: Each hemisegment contains 30 muscle cells that are organized into three main groups—dorsal, transverse, and ventral (Figure 1B).
evidence: Directly stated in text with reference to Figure 1B showing muscle organization.

claim: Each muscle group is targeted by non-overlapping sets of motor neurons.
source: Each muscle group is targeted by non-overlapping sets of motor neurons.
evidence: Directly stated in the text describing the organization of motor neuron targeting.

claim: By late larval stages Drosophila motor neuron-to-muscle synapses are large, experimentally-accessible, and extremely well-characterized.
source: Importantly, by late larval stages Drosophila motor neuron-to-muscle synapses are large, experimentally-accessible, and extremely well-characterized (Nose, 2012).
evidence: Stated in text with citation to Nose, 2012 supporting the characterization.

claim: Hunchback acting in NB7-1 controls the number of NB7-1 neuronal progeny that form functional synapses on dorsal muscles.
source: Previously, using the Drosophila motor system as a model, we found the classic temporal transcription factor Hunchback acts in NB7-1 neuronal stem cells to control the number of NB7-1 neuronal progeny form functional synapses on dorsal muscles (Meng et al., 2019).
evidence: Directly stated as a previous finding with citation to Meng et al., 2019.

claim: Prolonging expression of Hunchback in NB3-1 results in permanent alterations in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships.
source: Here, we perform additional temporal transcription factor manipulations—prolonging expression of Hunchback in NB3-1, as well as precociously expressing Pdm and Castor in NB7-1. We use confocal microscopy, calcium imaging, and electrophysiology to show that in every manipulation there are permanent alterations in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships.
evidence: Stated in abstract as a key finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Precociously expressing Pdm in NB7-1 results in permanent alterations in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships.
source: Here, we perform additional temporal transcription factor manipulations—prolonging expression of Hunchback in NB3-1, as well as precociously expressing Pdm and Castor in NB7-1. We use confocal microscopy, calcium imaging, and electrophysiology to show that in every manipulation there are permanent alterations in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships.
evidence: Stated in abstract as a key finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Precociously expressing Castor in NB7-1 results in permanent alterations in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships.
source: Here, we perform additional temporal transcription factor manipulations—prolonging expression of Hunchback in NB3-1, as well as precociously expressing Pdm and Castor in NB7-1. We use confocal microscopy, calcium imaging, and electrophysiology to show that in every manipulation there are permanent alterations in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships.
evidence: Stated in abstract as a key finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Temporal transcription factors, as a group of molecules, are potent determinants of synaptic partner choice and therefore ultimately control circuit membership.
source: Our data show temporal transcription factors, as a group of molecules, are potent determinants of synaptic partner choice and therefore ultimately control circuit membership.
evidence: Stated as the main conclusion in the abstract, based on the experimental findings.

claim: Circuit membership of neurons is determined by a series of decisions that impact many cell biological events.
source: Thus, circuit membership of neurons is determined by a series of decisions that impact many cell biological events.
evidence: Stated in the introduction as a conceptual framework for understanding circuit assembly.

claim: Motor neurons first decide to send axons out of the CNS; then axons decide to travel to a particular muscle field; once within a muscle field, axonal growth cones decide which muscle fiber to contact; and finally, growth cones decide to form functional synapses.
source: For example, motor neurons first decide to send axons out of the CNS; then axons decide to travel to a particular muscle field; once within a muscle field, axonal growth cones decide which muscle fiber to contact; and finally, growth cones decide to form functional synapses.
evidence: Stated as an example of the series of decisions neurons make during development.

claim: Temporal transcription factors have been postulated to control entire time-linked developmental programs.
source: This is because temporal transcription factors have been postulated to control entire time-linked developmental programs, and because in many systems there is a strong association between the birth time of a neuron and its ultimate circuit membership (Bhansali et al., 2014; Deguchi et al., 2011; Eerdunfu et al., 2017; Greaney et al., 2017; Jefferis et al., 2001; Kulkarni et al., 2016; McLean et al., 2007; McLean and Fetcho, 2009; Morrow et al., 2008; Osterhout et al., 2014; Petrovic and Hummel, 2008; Pujol-Martí et al., 2012; Tripodi et al., 2011; Li et al., 2013, Suzuki et al., 2013; Elliott et al., 2008; Alsiö et al., 2013; Doe, 2017; Allan and Thor, 2015; Wreden et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated with extensive citations supporting this postulate.

claim: In many systems there is a strong association between the birth time of a neuron and its ultimate circuit membership.
source: This is because temporal transcription factors have been postulated to control entire time-linked developmental programs, and because in many systems there is a strong association between the birth time of a neuron and its ultimate circuit membership (Bhansali et al., 2014; Deguchi et al., 2011; Eerdunfu et al., 2017; Greaney et al., 2017; Jefferis et al., 2001; Kulkarni et al., 2016; McLean et al., 2007; McLean and Fetcho, 2009; Morrow et al., 2008; Osterhout et al., 2014; Petrovic and Hummel, 2008; Pujol-Martí et al., 2012; Tripodi et al., 2011; Li et al., 2013, Suzuki et al., 2013; Elliott et al., 2008; Alsiö et al., 2013; Doe, 2017; Allan and Thor, 2015; Wreden et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated with extensive citations supporting this association.

claim: In many brain regions and model systems, temporal transcription factors control marker gene expression in newly-formed, post-mitotic neurons.
source: Consistent with the idea that temporal transcription factors control time-linked developmental programs, in many brain regions and model systems, temporal transcription factors control marker gene expression in newly-formed, post-mitotic neurons (Isshiki et al., 2001; Moris-Sanz et al., 2014; Novotny et al., 2002; Pearson and Doe, 2003; Tran and Doe, 2008; Cleary, 2006; Grosskortenhaus et al., 2006; Baumgardt et al., 2009; Stratmann et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated with multiple citations supporting this claim.

claim: Temporal transcription factors have been shown to control neurotransmitter phenotype.
source: This includes regulation of neurotransmitter phenotype (Stratmann and Thor, 2017; Isshiki et al., 2001; Allan and Thor, 2015), as well as regulation of axon pathfinding, dendrite targeting, and neuron morphology (Pearson and Doe, 2003; Seroka and Doe, 2019; Meng et al., 2019; Sullivan et al., 2019; Rossi et al., 2017; Doe, 2017).
evidence: Stated with citations to studies demonstrating this regulation.

claim: Temporal transcription factors have been shown to control axon pathfinding, dendrite targeting, and neuron morphology.
source: This includes regulation of neurotransmitter phenotype (Stratmann and Thor, 2017; Isshiki et al., 2001; Allan and Thor, 2015), as well as regulation of axon pathfinding, dendrite targeting, and neuron morphology (Pearson and Doe, 2003; Seroka and Doe, 2019; Meng et al., 2019; Sullivan et al., 2019; Rossi et al., 2017; Doe, 2017).
evidence: Stated with citations to studies demonstrating this regulation.

claim: Synapse formation is distinct from other aspects of neuronal maturation in that it is obligately non-cell autonomous because it requires two permissive partner cells to form a functional synapse.
source: Notably, synapse formation is distinct from other aspects of neuronal maturation in that it is obligately non-cell autonomous because it requires two permissive partner cells to form a functional synapse.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of synapse formation.

claim: Synapse formation may be particularly sensitive to dynamic environmental factors in developing animals.
source: Furthermore, synapse formation may be particularly sensitive to dynamic environmental factors in developing animals (e.g., availability of synaptic partners or transient signaling cues).
evidence: Stated as a speculation about the nature of synapse formation.

claim: Loss of the temporal transcription factor Eyeless/Pax6 impacted adult navigation behavior in Drosophila central complex.
source: A recent study in Drosophila central complex showed that loss of the temporal transcription factor Eyeless/Pax6 impacted the adult navigation behavior, demonstrating a long-lasting change in navigational circuits (Sullivan et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with citation to Sullivan et al., 2019.

claim: It is unknown how Eyeless alters neuronal function or whether it impacts synaptic partner selection.
source: However, it is unknown how Eyeless alters neuronal function, or whether it impacts synaptic partner selection.
evidence: Stated as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Prolonged expression of Hunchback in NB7-1 impacts motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic connections made by NB7-1 progeny.
source: Another recent study in Drosophila nerve cord showed prolonged expression of the temporal transcription factor Hunchback in neuroblast (NB) 7–1 neuronal stem cells impacts motor neuron-to muscle synaptic connections made by NB7-1 progeny (Meng et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with citation to Meng et al., 2019.

claim: Hunchback activity in NB7-1 controls synaptic partner choice.
source: These data demonstrate that Hunchback activity in NB7-1 controls synaptic partner choice.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from previous work.

claim: NB3-1 produces a series of ventrally-projecting, Hb9(+) RP motor neurons.
source: NB3-1 produces a series of ventrally-projecting, Hb9(+) RP motor neurons (Tran and Doe, 2008).
evidence: Stated with citation to Tran and Doe, 2008.

claim: NB3-1 generates four RP motor neurons in the following birth order: RP1, RP4, RP3, and RP5.
source: Specifically, NB3-1 generates four RP motor neurons in the following birth order: RP1, RP4, RP3, and RP5 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1C showing the lineage.

claim: All RP motor neurons express the transcription factor Hb9 and project to ventral muscles.
source: All RP motor neurons express the transcription factor Hb9 and project to ventral muscles (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: At larval stages, RP1, RP4, and RP3 make stable type one big (1b) neuromuscular synapses onto ventral Muscles 14, 30, and 6/7, respectively.
source: At larval stages, RP1, RP4, and RP3 make stable type one big (1b) neuromuscular synapses onto ventral Muscles 14, 30, and 6/7, respectively (Landgraf et al., 1997; Choi, 2004; Zarin et al., 2019; Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Stated with citations and reference to figures showing synaptic patterns.

claim: RP5 is a type one small (1s) motor neuron.
source: Here, we show RP5 is a type one small (1s) motor neuron (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Stated as a finding of this study with reference to figure showing the data.

claim: Dip-alpha-GAL4 drives GFP expression in 1s motor neurons.
source: To do so, we used a Dip-alpha-GAL4, which drives GFP expression in 1s motor neurons (herein Dip-alpha>GFP, Ashley et al., 2019; Pérez-Moreno and O'Kane, 2019), and we immunolabel RP1/4/3 (Hb9+, Kr+, Cut-) and RP5 (Hb9+, Kr-, Cut+) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: Stated with citations and reference to figures showing the expression pattern.

claim: Dip-alpha>GFP expression is specifically in RP5.
source: We find Dip-alpha>GFP expression specifically in RP5.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the immunolabeling experiment.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb embryos, there is an average of six ventral motor neurons (Hb9+, pMad+) that express markers characteristic of early-born RP motor neuron identity (RP1/RP4 Hb+, Kr+, Zfh2-, Cut-).
source: In NB3−1>Hb embryos, there is an average of six ventral motor neurons (Hb9+, pMad+), that express markers characteristic of early-born RP motor neuron identity (RP1/RP4 Hb+, Kr+, Zfh2-, Cut-), but not later-born RP motor neuron identity (RP3 Hb- Kr+ Zfh2+ Cut- and RP5 Hb- Kr- Zfh2+ Cut+) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,D–F).
evidence: Stated as a finding with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb embryos, there are no neurons with later-born RP motor neuron identity (RP3 Hb- Kr+ Zfh2+ Cut- and RP5 Hb- Kr- Zfh2+ Cut+).
source: In NB3−1>Hb embryos, there is an average of six ventral motor neurons (Hb9+, pMad+), that express markers characteristic of early-born RP motor neuron identity (RP1/RP4 Hb+, Kr+, Zfh2-, Cut-), but not later-born RP motor neuron identity (RP3 Hb- Kr+ Zfh2+ Cut- and RP5 Hb- Kr- Zfh2+ Cut+) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,D–F).
evidence: Stated as a finding with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Prolonged expression of Hunchback in NB3-1 increases the total number of ventral motor neurons at embryonic stages.
source: These data confirm that our reagents are working as expected. They show that prolonged expression of Hunchback in NB3-1 increases the total number of ventral motor neurons at embryonic stages.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the embryonic marker analysis.

claim: In wild-type, one 1b motor neuron makes one or two synaptic branches per muscle.
source: First, we counted the number of 1b and 1s synaptic branches on ventral muscles. In wild-type, one 1b motor neuron makes one or two synaptic branches per muscle (Figure 1C,E,L–P).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, there is a significant increase in the number of 1b synaptic branches onto Muscle 14 and 30 (RP1 and RP4 muscle targets, respectively).
source: In NB3−1>Hb, which has increased numbers of RP1/4 motor neurons compared to control, we find a significant increase in the number of 1b synaptic branch onto Muscle 14 and 30 (RP1 and RP4 muscle targets, respectively)(Figure 1D,H,M–N).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, there is a significant decrease in 1b branch number onto Muscles 6/7 (RP3 muscle target).
source: Additionally, in NB3−1>Hb, which has a decrease in numbers of RP3 and RP5 motor neurons, we see a significant decrease in 1b branch number onto Muscles 6/7 (RP3 muscle target) and a significant decrease in 1s branch number onto Muscle 12 (a RP5 muscle target) (Figures 1D,F,J,K,O–P).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, there is a significant decrease in 1s branch number onto Muscle 12 (a RP5 muscle target).
source: Additionally, in NB3−1>Hb, which has a decrease in numbers of RP3 and RP5 motor neurons, we see a significant decrease in 1b branch number onto Muscles 6/7 (RP3 muscle target) and a significant decrease in 1s branch number onto Muscle 12 (a RP5 muscle target) (Figures 1D,F,J,K,O–P).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified data.

claim: The alterations in embryonic RP motor neuron in NB3−1>Hb correlate with changes in the number of synaptic branches on ventral muscles at larval stages.
source: These data show that the alterations in embryonic RP motor neuron in NB3−1>Hb correlate with changes in the number of synaptic branches on ventral muscles at larval stages.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the anatomical analysis.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, in comparison to controls, there is normal abundance and localization for pre-synaptic active zone marker (Bruchpilot), a post-synaptic marker (Discs large), and a post-synaptic neurotransmitter receptor (GluRIIA).
source: To do so, we stained for pre-synaptic active zone marker (Bruchpilot), a post-synaptic marker (Discs large), and a post-synaptic neurotransmitter receptor (GluRIIA) (Figure 2A). In NB3−1>Hb, in comparison to controls, we find normal abundance and localization for all markers (Figure 2C–H).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing the immunostaining data.

claim: The extra synaptic branches on ventral muscles in NB3−1>Hb contain functional synapses.
source: These data strongly suggest that the extra synaptic branches on ventral muscles in NB3−1>Hb contain functional synapses.
evidence: Stated as an inference from the synaptic marker data.

claim: Prolonged expression of Hb in NB3-1 leads to long-lasting changes in motor neuron-to-muscles synapses.
source: We conclude prolonged expression of Hb in NB3-1 leads to long-lasting changes in motor neuron-to-muscles synapses.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the anatomical and molecular analyses.

claim: In the Drosophila motor system, there exist well-characterized, homeostatic mechanisms that keep the muscle's response to nerve stimulation within a set range of values.
source: In the Drosophila motor system, there exist well-characterized, homeostatic mechanisms that keep the muscle's response to nerve stimulation within a set range of values (Frank et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated with citation to Frank et al., 2020.

claim: Anatomical changes do not necessarily lead to functional alterations in the Drosophila motor system.
source: This means that anatomical changes do not necessarily lead to functional alterations.
evidence: Stated as a consequence of homeostatic mechanisms.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, there is no increase in EPSP amplitude on Muscle 30 compared to wild type.
source: However, we observe no increase in EPSP amplitude in NB3−1>Hb, compared to wild type (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing electrophysiology data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, there is a significant increase in quantal content on Muscle 30 when compared to control animals.
source: In NB3−1>Hb, there is a significant increase in quantal content when compared to control animals (Figure 3F).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified electrophysiology data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, there is a significant decrease in mEPSP amplitude on Muscle 30 compared to control animals.
source: However, in NB3−1>Hb, there is a significant decrease in mEPSP amplitude compared to control animals (Figure 3C,E).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified electrophysiology data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb on Muscle 30, the postsynaptic receptor sensitivity to neurotransmitter is reduced.
source: These data suggest that the postsynaptic receptor sensitivity to neurotransmitter is reduced.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the decreased mEPSP amplitude.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, Muscle 6 has a significant decrease in EPSP amplitude compared to control.
source: Our data are consistent with these expectations (Figure 3H–K).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing electrophysiology data for Muscle 6.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, Muscle 6 has a significant decrease in quantal content compared to control.
source: Our data are consistent with these expectations (Figure 3H–K).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing electrophysiology data for Muscle 6.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, there is impaired synaptic function and lack of homeostatic compensation on Muscle 6.
source: Thus, in NB3−1>Hb, there is impaired synaptic function and lack of homeostatic compensation on Muscle 6.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the electrophysiology data.

claim: In NB3−1>Hb, on Muscle 30, there are wild type levels of synaptic function.
source: We conclude that in NB3−1>Hb, on Muscle 30, there are wild type levels of synaptic function.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the electrophysiology data.

claim: Prolonged expression of Hunchback in NB3-1 results in functional changes in motor system physiology.
source: Taken together these data show that prolonged expression of Hunchback in NB3-1 results in functional changes in motor system physiology.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the electrophysiology experiments.

claim: In the Drosophila motor system, Hunchback is one of several temporal transcription factors in a well-characterized cascade that also includes Kruppel, Pdm, and Cas.
source: In the Drosophila motor system, Hunchback is one of several temporal transcription factors in a well-characterized cascade that also includes Kruppel, Pdm, and Cas (Doe, 2017).
evidence: Stated with citation to Doe, 2017.

claim: Hunchback is the earliest transcription factor in the temporal transcription factor cascade.
source: First, Hunchback is the earliest transcription factor in the cascade, whereas Castor and Pdm are expressed later in the cascade.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of Hunchback.

claim: Castor and Pdm are expressed later in the temporal transcription factor cascade than Hunchback.
source: First, Hunchback is the earliest transcription factor in the cascade, whereas Castor and Pdm are expressed later in the cascade.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of Castor and Pdm.

claim: Hunchback is thought to specify early-born temporal identities.
source: Second, Hunchback is thought to specify early-born temporal identities, whereas Castor and Pdm specify later-born temporal identities.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of Hunchback.

claim: Castor and Pdm specify later-born temporal identities.
source: Second, Hunchback is thought to specify early-born temporal identities, whereas Castor and Pdm specify later-born temporal identities.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of Castor and Pdm.

claim: Prolonged expression of Hunchback extends the time that neuroblasts produce early-born neurons.
source: Third, prolonged expression of Hunchback extends the time that neuroblasts produce early-born neurons, whereas precocious expression of Castor and Pdm can truncate the time that neuroblasts produce early-born neurons.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of Hunchback manipulation.

claim: Precocious expression of Castor and Pdm can truncate the time that neuroblasts produce early-born neurons.
source: Third, prolonged expression of Hunchback extends the time that neuroblasts produce early-born neurons, whereas precocious expression of Castor and Pdm can truncate the time that neuroblasts produce early-born neurons.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of Castor and Pdm manipulation.

claim: Early divisions of NB7-1 give rise to five U motor neurons in the following birth order: U1, U2, U3, U4, and U5.
source: Early divisions of NB7-1 give rise to five U motor neurons in the following birth order: U1, U2, U3, U4, and U5 (Figure 4A).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing the lineage.

claim: All U motor neurons express the transcription factor Eve and synapse on dorsal muscles.
source: All U motor neurons express the transcription factor Eve and synapse on dorsal muscles (Figure 4A).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing the lineage and synaptic patterns.

claim: In embryos, each U motor neuron can be identified by a unique combination of marker genes.
source: In embryos, each U motor neuron can be identified by a unique combination of marker genes, and in larvae, each U motor neuron forms a synapse on a unique dorsal muscle (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing molecular markers.

claim: In larvae, each U motor neuron forms a synapse on a unique dorsal muscle.
source: In embryos, each U motor neuron can be identified by a unique combination of marker genes, and in larvae, each U motor neuron forms a synapse on a unique dorsal muscle (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing synaptic patterns.

claim: In wild type, in NB7-1, Cas is first expressed during the division that generates the U5 motor neuron.
source: In wild type, in NB7-1, Cas is first expressed during the division that generates the U5 motor neuron, and Cas continues to be expressed in NB7-1 during subsequent divisions that give rise to a set of Cas(+) interneurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing the lineage.

claim: Cas expression closes the window of U motor neuron production.
source: Cas expression closes the window of U motor neuron production.
evidence: Stated as a function of Cas in the lineage.

claim: In a majority of hemisegments in NB7−1>Cas, there are decreases to sets of three or four U motor neurons.
source: In a majority of hemisegments in NB7−1>Cas, we see decreases to sets of three or four U motor neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: In NB7−1>Cas, U motor neuron sets have molecular identities of U1, U2, U3 or U1, U2, U3, U4/U5.
source: These U motor neuron sets have molecular identities of U1, U2, U3 or U1, U2, U3, U4/U5, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing molecular marker data.

claim: At embryonic stages, precocious expression of Cas, specifically in NB7-1, decreases the number of U motor neurons.
source: We conclude that at embryonic stages, precocious expression of Cas, specifically in NB7-1, decreases the number of U motor neurons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the embryonic marker analysis.

claim: In hemisegments in NB7−1>Cas with three or four U motor neurons, there is no change in 1b branch number onto Muscles 9, 10, and 2 (U1, U2, and U3 muscle targets, respectively) compared to controls.
source: Compared to controls, we find no change in 1b branch number onto Muscles 9, 10, and 2 (U1, U2, and U3 muscle targets, respectively) (Figure 4E–H,K–L).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified data.

claim: In hemisegments in NB7−1>Cas with three or four U motor neurons, there is a significant decrease in 1b branch number onto Muscles 3 and 4 (U4 and U5 muscle targets, respectively) compared to controls.
source: However, compared to our control, we see a significant decrease in 1b branch number onto Muscles 3 and 4 (U4 and U5 muscle targets, respectively) (Figure 4I–J,M–N).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified data.

claim: Precocious expression of Cas in NB7-1 leads to changes in embryonic U motor neuron number, and these changes correspond to long-lasting changes in motor neuron-to-dorsal muscle synapses at larval stages.
source: These data suggest that precocious expression of Cas in NB7-1 leads to changes in embryonic U motor neuron number, and that these changes correspond to long-lasting changes in motor neuron-to-dorsal muscle synapses at larval stages.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the anatomical analysis.

claim: At least one temporal transcription factor other than Hunchback can control motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships.
source: We conclude that at least one temporal transcription factor other than Hunchback can control motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the Castor manipulation experiments.

claim: Pdm is expressed during the fourth and fifth division window of NB7-1.
source: We manipulate Pdm, which is expressed during the fourth and fifth division window of NB7-1 (Figure 5A).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing the lineage.

claim: Pdm specifies the U4 temporal identity and represses Kruppel.
source: Pdm specifies the U4 temporal identity and represses Kruppel, the temporal transcription factor that specifies the U3 temporal identity (Grosskortenhaus et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated with citation to Grosskortenhaus et al., 2006.

claim: In NB7−1>Pdm, there are two phenotypes--either decreases or increases in the number of U motor neurons per abdominal hemisegment in comparison to controls.
source: Specifically, in NB7−1>Pdm, we see two phenotypes--either decreases or increases in the number of U motor neurons per abdominal hemisegment in comparison to controls (Figure 5B–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: In NB7−1>Pdm, hemisegments with additional U motor neurons are observed selectively in segments A1-A3.
source: Notably, we observe this phenotype selectively in segments A1-A3 (Figure 5B).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing the data.

claim: In NB7−1>Pdm segments A1-A3, U motor neurons have the following embryonic molecular identities: U1, U2, U3, U4, followed by a variable number of U5-like neurons.
source: In these segments, U motor neurons have the following embryonic molecular identities: U1, U2, U3, U4, followed by a variable number of U5-like neurons (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–G).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing molecular marker data.

claim: In NB7−1>Pdm, hemisegments with fewer U motor neurons are observed selectively in segments A4-A7.
source: Notably, we observe this phenotype selectively in segments A4-A7 (Figure 5C).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing the data.

claim: In NB7−1>Pdm segments A4-A7, U motor neurons have the following embryonic molecular identities: U1, U2, U4, and U5, but not U3.
source: In these segments, U motor neurons have the following embryonic molecular identities: U1, U2, U4, and U5, but not U3 (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing molecular marker data.

claim: In NB7−1>Pdm at embryonic stage late 11 to early 12, of the four Eve(+) neurons two can be Runt(+).
source: In NB7−1>Pdm, at the same stage, of the four Eve(+) neurons two can be Runt(+) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure showing the data.

claim: When hemisegments in NB7−1>Pdm contain >5 Eve(+) pMad(+) neurons, there is a significant increase in 1b branch number selectively on Muscle 4.
source: When hemisegments contain >5 Eve(+) pMad(+) neurons (e.g., those with U5-like neurons born at abnormally late times), we find a significant increase in 1b branch number selectively Muscle 4 (i.e., wild type U5 target, Figure 5B,K,P), while all other muscles had no change in branch number compared to our control (Figure 5).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified data.

claim: When hemisegments in NB7−1>Pdm contain 4 Eve(+) pMad(+) neurons, there is a significant decrease in 1b branch number on Muscle 2 (U3 muscle target) compared to control.
source: When hemisegments contain 4 Eve(+) pMad(+) neurons (e.g., those with U4 and U5 generated at abnormally early time and lacking a U3-like neuron), compared to our control, we find a significant decrease in 1b branch number on Muscle 2 (U3 muscle target, Figure 5C,I,N), and no changes in 1b branch number on other muscles (Figure 5).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing quantified data.

claim: The alterations in embryonic motor neuron markers in NB7−1 > Pdm correlates with changes in the number of synaptic branches on dorsal muscles at larval stages.
source: These data show that the alterations in embryonic motor neuron markers in NB7−1 > Pdm correlates with changes in the number of synaptic branches on dorsal muscles at larval stages.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the anatomical analysis.

claim: In NB7−1>Pdm in abdominal segments A1-A3, the increased nerve branches on Muscle 4 have normal abundance and localization for synaptic proteins Bruchpilot, Discs large, and GluRIIA.
source: We find a normal abundance and localization for all markers (Figure 6B–G).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing immunostaining data.

claim: On the cell biological level, neuromuscular synapses in NB7−1>Pdm are not different from Control.
source: Thus, on the cell biological level, neuromuscular synapses in NB7−1>Pdm are not different from Control.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the synaptic marker analysis.

claim: In both Control and NB7−1>Pdm, within a five-minute imaging period, there is at least one postsynaptic response on Muscle 4.
source: In both Control and NB7−1>Pdm, we see that within a five-minute imaging period, there is at least one postsynaptic response (Figure 6H–I, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing calcium imaging data.

claim: Pdm can impact functional synaptic connections onto muscles made by U motor neurons.
source: From these findings, we conclude that Pdm can impact functional synaptic connections onto muscles made by U motor neurons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the calcium imaging experiments.

claim: Precocious expression of Pdm in NB7-1 leads to two different types of heterochronic mismatches: one in which later-born U motor neurons are born at abnormally late times in development, and one in which later-born U motor neurons are born at abnormally early times in development.
source: In summary, we find that precocious expression of Pdm in NB7-1 leads to two different types of heterochronic mismatches: one in which later-born U motor neurons are born at abnormally late times in development, and one in which later-born U motor neurons are born at abnormally early times in development.
evidence: Stated as a summary of the Pdm manipulation findings.

claim: There is a strong correlation between embryonic molecular identity and larval neuromuscular synapses in NB7−1>Pdm.
source: We find a strong correlation between embryonic molecular identity and larval neuromuscular synapses.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: Regardless of birth time, both early-born and later-born U motor neurons can target specific dorsal muscles.
source: Together these data support the idea that regardless of birth time, both early-born and later-born U motor neurons can target specific dorsal muscles.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the heterochronic mismatch experiments.

claim: Hb is not the only temporal transcription factor that can provide enough molecular information to neuronal progeny, such that the neuronal progeny are insensitive to time-linked environmental cues.
source: They demonstrate that Hb is not the only temporal transcription that can provide enough molecular information to neuronal progeny, such that the neuronal progeny are insensitive to time-linked environmental cues.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: A general feature of the temporal transcription factors is to control neuromuscular synapse formation.
source: Ultimately this supports the idea that a general feature of the temporal transcription factors is to control neuromuscular synapse formation.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: Prolonged expression of the temporal transcription factor, Hunchback increases the number of RP motor neurons produced by NB3-1 and permanently changes the functional innervation of ventral muscles.
source: First, we find prolonged expression of the temporal transcription factor, Hunchback increases the number of RP motor neurons produced by NB3-1 and that this manipulation permanently changes the functional innervation of ventral muscles (Figures 1–3).
evidence: Stated as a key finding in the discussion with reference to figures.

claim: A general feature of Hunchback is to control motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships.
source: Because we previously showed that Hunchback acts similarly in another neuroblast, NB7-1, we conclude that a general feature of Hunchback is to control motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships (Meng et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion combining current and previous findings.

claim: Precocious expression of temporal transcription factors, Castor and Pdm, alter the number of U motor neurons produced by NB7-1 and permanently change the functional innervation of dorsal muscles.
source: Second, we find precocious expression of temporal transcription factors, Castor and Pdm, alter the number of U motor neurons produced by NB7-1 and permanently change the functional innervation of dorsal muscles (Figures 4–6).
evidence: Stated as a key finding in the discussion with reference to figures.

claim: Temporal transcription factors, as a class of molecules, are potent regulators of synaptic partner selection.
source: Together these findings provide strong support for the hypothesis that temporal transcription factors, as a class of molecules, are potent regulators of synaptic partner selection.
evidence: Stated as the main conclusion of the study.

claim: In Drosophila motor system development, most neuroblasts express the temporal transcription factor Hunchback early during lineage development.
source: In Drosophila motor system development, most neuroblasts express the temporal transcription factor Hunchback early during lineage development (Pearson and Doe, 2004).
evidence: Stated with citation to Pearson and Doe, 2004.

claim: In all of the multiple lineages tested so far, Hunchback is necessary and sufficient to specify early-born neuronal marker gene expression, regardless of the cell type.
source: In all of the multiple lineages tested so far, Hunchback is necessary and sufficient to specify early-born neuronal marker gene expression, regardless of the cell type (e.g., motor neuron, interneuron, glia) (Cleary, 2006; Isshiki et al., 2001; Kambadur et al., 1998; Novotny et al., 2002; Pearson and Doe, 2003).
evidence: Stated with multiple citations supporting this claim.

claim: The mammalian homolog of Hunchback, Ikaros, regulates early-born marker gene expression in both retina and cortex.
source: Notably, the mammalian homolog of Hunchback, Ikaros, similarly regulates early-born marker gene expression in both retina and cortex (Alsiö et al., 2013; Elliott et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with citations to Alsiö et al., 2013 and Elliott et al., 2008.

claim: In the Drosophila nerve cord, in multiple lineages, Hunchback regulates embryonic axonal trajectory.
source: In the Drosophila nerve cord, in multiple lineages, Hunchback regulates other aspects of time-linked, post-mitotic neuronal identity, including embryonic axonal trajectory (Isshiki et al., 2001; Tran and Doe, 2008; Seroka and Doe, 2019; Meng et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with multiple citations supporting this claim.

claim: NB3-1 begins dividing much later in nerve cord development than NB7-1.
source: Notably, NB3-1 begins dividing much later in nerve cord development than NB7-1 (Bossing et al., 1996).
evidence: Stated with citation to Bossing et al., 1996.

claim: Prolonging the expression of Hunchback in NB3-1 dramatically increased the number of Hb9(+) motor neurons produced and caused permanent changes in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships and physiology in the ventral muscle circuit.
source: Prolonging the expression of Hunchback in NB3-1 dramatically increased the number of Hb9(+) motor neurons produced and caused permanent changes in neuromuscular synaptic partnerships and physiology in the ventral muscle circuit (Figures 1–3).
evidence: Stated with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Hunchback controls muscle targeting of motor neurons consistently across two lineages (NB3-1 and NB7-1).
source: First, Hunchback controls muscle targeting of motor neurons consistently across two lineages.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from comparing NB3-1 and NB7-1 results.

claim: Muscles that are over-innervated in comparison to control can have normal synaptic transmission.
source: Second, muscles that are over-innervated in comparison to control can have normal synaptic transmission, but muscles that are under-innervated, in comparison to control, have impaired synaptic physiology.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the electrophysiology experiments.

claim: Muscles that are under-innervated, in comparison to control, have impaired synaptic physiology.
source: Second, muscles that are over-innervated in comparison to control can have normal synaptic transmission, but muscles that are under-innervated, in comparison to control, have impaired synaptic physiology.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the electrophysiology experiments.

claim: Hunchback controls synaptic partner selection consistently across different time points in nerve cord development.
source: Third, Hunchback controls synaptic partner selection consistently across different time points in nerve cord development.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from comparing NB3-1 and NB7-1 which divide at different times.

claim: In many lineages Hunchback is likely to regulate synaptic partner selection.
source: This suggests that in many lineages Hunchback is likely to regulate synaptic partner selection, which has broader implications extending to Hunchback's vertebrate ortholog, Ikaros (Mattar et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as a speculation based on the findings, with citation to Mattar et al., 2015.

claim: A Castor homolog, Casz1, has been shown to be a temporal transcription factor in vertebrates.
source: In vertebrates, a Castor homolog, Casz1, has also been shown to be a temporal transcription factor (Mattar et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citation to Mattar et al., 2015.

claim: In wild type, NB7-1 produces five U motor neurons, each of which can be uniquely identified by embryonic molecular markers, and each of which, in larvae, makes a unique motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnership.
source: In wild type, NB7-1 produces five U motor neurons, each of which can be uniquely identified by embryonic molecular markers, and each of which, in larvae, makes a unique motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnership.
evidence: Stated as background information about the NB7-1 lineage.

claim: In NB7−1 > Cas, the embryonic molecular identities that are lost are U4 and U5.
source: Notably, in NB7−1 > Cas, the embryonic molecular identities that are lost are U4 and U5.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the Castor manipulation experiments.

claim: In NB7−1 > Cas larval stages, the specific dorsal muscles that are under innervated are the normal U4 and U5 target muscles.
source: In larval stages, the specific dorsal muscles that are under innervated are the normal U4 and U5 target muscles.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the Castor manipulation experiments.

claim: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A1-A3, the U3 embryonic molecular identity is skipped.
source: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A1-A3, the U3 embryonic molecular identity is skipped, and in larval stages the normal U3 muscle is under-innervated.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A1-A3, in larval stages the normal U3 muscle is under-innervated.
source: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A1-A3, the U3 embryonic molecular identity is skipped, and in larval stages the normal U3 muscle is under-innervated.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A4-A7, extra U5 embryonic identities are produced.
source: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A4-A7, extra U5 embryonic identities are produced, and in larval stages the normal U5 target is over-innervated.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A4-A7, in larval stages the normal U5 target is over-innervated.
source: In NB7−1 > Pdm, in segments A4-A7, extra U5 embryonic identities are produced, and in larval stages the normal U5 target is over-innervated.
evidence: Stated as a finding from the Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: In both NB7−1 > Cas and NB7−1 > Pdm there is strong correlation between embryonic molecular identity and mature motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships.
source: Thus, in both NB7−1 > Cas and NB7−1 > Pdm there is strong correlation between embryonic molecular identity and mature motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the Castor and Pdm manipulation experiments.

claim: In previous work, which prolonged Hunchback in NB7-1, there was a poor correlation between embryonic molecular identity markers and mature motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships.
source: This finding is somewhat surprising given that in previous work, which prolonged Hunchback in NB7-1, there was a poor correlation between embryonic molecular identity markers and mature motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships (Meng et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with citation to Meng et al., 2019.

claim: The predominant model states that temporal transcription factors are master regulators of entire temporal programs, and should therefore determine not just early neuronal features like marker gene expression, but also terminal neuronal features such as synaptic partner selection.
source: Notably the correlation between embryonic molecular identity and synaptic partnerships seen in this study using Cas and Pdm manipulation is more inline with the predominant model in the field. The predominant model states that temporal transcription factors are master regulators of entire temporal programs, and should therefore determine not just early neuronal features like marker gene expression, but also terminal neuronal features such as synaptic partner selection.
evidence: Stated as a description of the predominant model in the field.

claim: There is variability in the predictive strength of molecular identity markers.
source: Overall, our data demonstrate that there is variability in the predictive strength of molecular identity markers.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from comparing different temporal transcription factor manipulations.

claim: Data in NB7−1 > Pdm support a model in which lineage intrinsic factors determine motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships regardless of environmental cues present.
source: Our data in NB7−1 > Pdm, support a model in which lineage intrinsic factors determine motor neuron-to-muscle synaptic partnerships regardless of environmental cues present.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the heterochronic mismatch experiments.

claim: The heterochronic mismatches studied so far are on the order of one to several neuroblast divisions, or hours.
source: First, the time scale of heterochronic mismatches studied so far is on the order of one to several neuroblast divisions, or hours.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of the current study.

claim: It is unknown how heterochronic mismatches conducted at larger time scales would impact the system.
source: So, it is unknown how heterochronic mismatches conducted at larger time scales would impact the system.
evidence: Stated as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Motor neuron-to-muscle synapses are distinct from neuron-neuron synapses in the CNS, in that motor neuron-to-muscle synapses are usually one-to-one partnerships, and because motor neuron axonal targets are large, pre-existing muscles.
source: Second, so far the heterochronic mismatches performed in the Drosophila motor system have focused on neuromuscular synapses as a readout. Neuromuscular synapses are distinct from neuron-neuron synapses in the CNS, in that motor neuron-to-muscle synapses are usually one-to-one partnerships, and because motor neuron axonal targets are large, pre-existing muscles.
evidence: Stated as a distinguishing feature of neuromuscular synapses.

claim: Manipulation of Pdm produces two different phenotypes that are correlated with anterior-posterior (A-P) position.
source: We note that manipulation of Pdm produces two different phenotypes (Figure 5). How does one manipulation give two opposing phenotypes? We find that the different phenotypes are correlated with anterior-posterior (A-P) position, raising the possibility that this difference involves factors differentially expressed along A-P axis (e.g., Hox genes).
evidence: Stated as an observation with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Converging mechanisms leading to one molecular identity could occur within one class of stem cell (e.g., NB7-1) found at different A-P positions.
source: Our data raise the possibility that converging mechanisms leading to one molecular identity could occur within one class of stem cell (e.g., NB7-1) found at different A-P positions.
evidence: Stated as a speculation based on the Pdm manipulation findings.

claim: The Drosophila motor system contains circuits that control synergistic groups of muscles.
source: The Drosophila motor system contains circuits that control synergistic groups of muscles (Clark et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated with citation to Clark et al., 2018.

claim: One circuit controls contraction of dorsal muscles, one circuit controls transverse muscles, and one circuit controls ventral muscles.
source: One circuit controls contraction of dorsal muscles, one circuit controls transverse muscles, and one circuit controls ventral muscles (Mesoderm, 1993; Heckscher et al., 2012; Zarin et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with citations supporting this organization.

claim: Early in development, NB7-1 generates motor neurons which project to dorsal muscles and populate the dorsal muscle circuit.
source: Early in development, NB7-1 generates motor neurons which project to dorsal muscles and populate the dorsal muscle circuit.
evidence: Stated as background information about NB7-1 lineage development.

claim: Later in development, NB7-1 generates interneurons, which do not project out of the CNS and do not populate the dorsal muscle circuit.
source: Later in development, NB7-1 generates interneurons, which do not project out of the CNS and do not populate the dorsal muscle circuit (Mark et al., 2019; Schmid et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated with citations to Mark et al., 2019 and Schmid et al., 1999.

claim: Early in development, NB3-1 generates motor neurons which project to ventral muscles and populate the ventral muscle circuit, and later it generates interneurons.
source: Similarly, early in development, NB3-1 generates motor neurons which project to ventral muscles and populate the ventral muscle circuit, and later it generates interneurons (Schmid et al., 1999; Figure 7A).
evidence: Stated with citation to Schmid et al., 1999 and reference to figure.

claim: Temporal transcription factors can be thought of as molecular switches acting in the neuroblast to regulate circuit membership of neuronal progeny.
source: We suggest temporal transcription factors can be thought of as molecular switches acting in the neuroblast to regulate circuit membership of neuronal progeny.
evidence: Stated as a conceptual model based on the findings.

claim: Prolonging the expression of Hunchback in NB7-1 dramatically increases the number of Eve(+) U motor neurons without changing the total number of neurons produced by the lineage.
source: First, a pair of recent studies showed that prolonging the expression of Hunchback in NB7-1 dramatically increases the number of Eve(+) U motor neurons without changing the total number of neurons produced by the lineage (Seroka and Doe, 2019; Meng et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with citations to Seroka and Doe, 2019 and Meng et al., 2019.

claim: The extra U motor neurons in NB7-1>Hb form permanent, functional synapses on dorsal muscles.
source: The extra U motor neurons form permanent, functional synapses on dorsal muscles (Meng et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated with citation to Meng et al., 2019.

claim: In NB7-1, Hunchback determines what proportion of neurons from the lineage populate the dorsal muscle circuit.
source: Therefore, in NB7-1, Hunchback determines what proportion of neurons from the lineage populate the dorsal muscle circuit.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the Hunchback manipulation in NB7-1.

claim: Temporal transcription factors can bi-directionally modulate the proportion of neurons from a lineage that populate a given motor circuit.
source: Thus, temporal transcription factors can bi-directionally modulate the proportion of neurons from a lineage that populate a given motor circuit.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the various temporal transcription factor manipulations.

claim: It is possible that temporal transcription factors in other parts of the Drosophila CNS, and vertebrate orthologs of the temporal transcription factors manipulated in this study, regulate circuit membership decisions in similar ways.
source: It is possible that temporal transcription factors in other parts of the Drosophila CNS, and vertebrate orthologs of the temporal transcription factors manipulated in this study, regulate circuit membership decisions in similar ways.
evidence: Stated as a speculation about the broader implications of the findings.
